name: Passkeys in an app (create and sign in)
plain: Creates and uses phishing resistant passkeys for sign in inside an app.
meaning: Replaces passwords with device-held keys; an app learns only a public key, never the biometric. Passkeys sync through the platform keychain, so account recovery shifts to Google or Apple.

android.permission: None (Credential Manager API 34; Jetpack back to Android 4.4 with Play services passkeys on 9+)
android.prompt_ui: Bottom sheet: Create passkey / Use saved passkey with biometric confirm
android.persistence: Syncs across devices through Google Password Manager
android.revocation: Settings > Passwords & accounts > Google Password Manager
android.note: Digital Asset Links bind app and domain (assetlinks.json); Android 14 adds credential provider support.

ios.prompt_ui: Sheet with passkey and Face ID or Touch ID confirm
ios.note: iOS 17 adds passkey manager providers and conditional UI; iOS 26 adds passkey import and export between providers.

limits.headline: Can create and use passkeys inside the app after you approve with your device lock
limits.user_action: You tap Create a passkey or Sign in with a passkey, then confirm with fingerprint, face or PIN
can: Create a passkey for your account tied to the app and its website
Sign you in with a passkey instead of a password
Show a system sheet listing the passkeys you already have
Sync passkeys through your password manager or cloud keychain
cannot: See your private passkey or your screen lock
Use a passkey without your approval each time
Use the passkey on a different website or app than it was made for
Work on very old phones without Google Play services (Android)
limits.reach_label: One approved sign in at a time
limits.differs: Android uses Credential Manager. iPhone needs the app tied to its website and supports other managers from iOS 17.

story.what_it_is: You sign in with a face or fingerprint scan instead of a password.

marketing.name: Passkeys
marketing.pitch: Sign in with Face ID or Touch ID instead of passwords, and passkeys sync across your Apple devices.

marketing.name: Passkeys
marketing.pitch: Android and Google make passkeys the simple, safer way to sign in without remembering passwords.

story.for_you: You tap sign in, glance at your phone or touch the sensor, and you are in. No password to remember or type. A fake site cannot steal it because the passkey only works on the real one.
story.for_makers: Makers see fewer password resets, fewer stolen accounts and quicker sign ups. It also moves the key storage to Apple or Google, so recovery and lock in become the platform's problem and power.

use_cases.example: A shop lets you create a passkey after your first order, then logs you in next time with a face scan.
A bank swaps password and text code for a passkey, which cuts phishing losses.
A game platform signs you in with a passkey so a hacked reused password cannot steal your skins.
A social app lets you sign in with a passkey from your tablet through the shared keychain.
An airline app signs you in with a passkey, so you check in fast at the airport.
A company login uses passkeys so staff stop falling for fake login pages.

risks: Recovery depends on Google or Apple
story.android_note: Android stores passkeys in Google Password Manager or a chosen provider and syncs them to your other Android devices.
story.ios_note: iPhone stores passkeys in iCloud Keychain, and since iOS 17 other apps can offer to hold them too.

technical_bounds: Both vendors sync keys with their own cloud
